description:
Verified 2026-08-30: the telemetry emit/dispatch layer is raw-and-free as
designed (refs only; no-handler dispatch = empty-vec loop), but the scheduler
builds the CAUSALITY RECORDS unconditionally: AppliedStep.wakes (one Wake per
wake, cause cloned, dedup removed by fz-kdt.34.3) and AppliedStep.blocked.
Their only production consumer is wakes.is_empty() (drive-loop quiescence
check); changed/movements have real production consumers (fact table, memo
reconcile) and are not this ticket.

Measured cost (release, 00420, A/B with records capped at 1/step, stdout
identical): 550.7 -> 543.3 ms median, ranges overlapping -- <=1.3%, likely
under 1%.

Fix directions, if ever worth the point:
(a) a tel.wants(prefix) query letting the scheduler skip record ASSEMBLY when
    no handler subscribes to work_graph -- still zero rendering at emit,
    behavior identical, contract restored fully; or
(b) production keeps a woke bool; handlers reconstruct wakes from
    deps.subscribers x changed -- REJECTED on inspection: disposition
    (enqueued/coalesced) is transient scheduler state at wake time and not
    reconstructible later.
Do not spend more than the ~1% is worth; this ticket exists so the measured
exception to the raw-boundary contract is on record, not to force the fix.
title: AppliedStep wake/blocked records are built with telemetry off: ~1% of compile
